_template_meta.reviewed_by: Knowledge Base / Data Engineering, then Clinical
instructions: Copy this file to proposals/<yyyy-mm-dd>-<short-name>.json and fill in `entries`.
One object per proposed vocabulary entry. Delete this _template_meta block in the copy.
Every field marked required must be filled. `null` is not a value for a required field.
An entry with approval_status other than 'approved' MUST NOT enter a release artifact. tools/validate_vocabulary.py rejects unreviewed content in a candidate marked for publication.

Proposing an ALIAS is cheap and is the default. Proposing a NEW TOKEN is expensive: it is a clinical_token_identity change, blocks publication pending clinical review, and needs regression cases. Prefer an alias unless the concept is genuinely clinically distinct.

Do not propose an alias that is merely a spelling variant the normalizer already handles. Check first: python3 -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'tools'); from vocab.normalize import normalize; print(normalize('your phrase'))"

request.rationale: <required — why this expansion is needed; what user problem it solves>
request.target_artifact_version: <required — the vocabulary version this is intended to land in>

entries.proposal_type: <required — one of: alias | new_token | body_area_association | complaint_group | severity_applicability | duration_applicability | deprecation>
entries.existing_token_id: <required for everything except new_token — the token this attaches to>
entries.proposed_canonical_label: <required — caregiver-facing plain English, max 80 chars. Not clinical jargon. 'Skin pulling in between the ribs when breathing', not 'chest indrawing'.>
proposed_aliases: <0..n search phrases users would actually type or say>
entries.intended_body_area: <required or null — must be one of body_area_tokens; see the vocabulary artifact>

descriptors: <0..n values from severity_tokens — descriptive only, changes no weight or urgency tier>

entries.complaint_group: <required or null — an existing complaint_group_id, or a proposed new one>
entries.ambiguity_notes: <required — what else could a user mean by this phrase? Name every existing token it could plausibly collide with. Write 'none identified' only after actually checking; leaving this thin is the single most common way an unsafe alias gets through.>
known_collisions: <0..n existing token_ids whose canonical label or alias set this would collide with after normalization>
entries.collision_is_intended: <required if known_collisions is non-empty — true means 'this SHOULD produce an ambiguity prompt'; false means the proposal needs rewording>
entries.source_provenance: <required — where this wording came from. A named clinical source, a user-research session with a date, a WHO/IMCI/NCDC document with a section reference. 'Seemed sensible' is not provenance.>
entries.clinical_reviewer: <required for approval — name of the clinician who reviewed this entry>
entries.approval_status: <required — one of: draft | in_review | approved | rejected>
entries.approval_evidence: <required when approval_status is 'approved' — PR URL, issue URL, or signed document reference. A claim with no link is not an approval.>
affected_existing_tokens: <0..n token_ids whose behaviour or reachability this changes>
affected_questions_or_rules: <0..n rule_ids or question identifiers this touches. Any non-empty value here escalates the change beyond search-only metadata.>

regression_cases_required.rationale: <why this case proves the change is safe>

entries.expected_change_classification: <required — the class you expect tools/classify_vocabulary_diff.py to assign: search_only_metadata | display_only_metadata | clinical_token_identity | red_flag_affecting | scoring_rule_affecting | question_flow_affecting | deprecation_removal>

_submission_checklist: Every required field is filled — no placeholder text remains.
ambiguity_notes reflects an actual check against the existing 295 tokens, not a guess.
No proposed alias merely restates a spelling variant normalization already handles.
No proposed alias shadows another token's canonical form unless collision_is_intended is true.
Every entry with approval_status 'approved' has a named clinical_reviewer, a review_date and a resolvable approval_evidence link.
Any entry whose expected_change_classification is a blocking class has regression_cases_required filled in.
The request has been run past Knowledge Base / Data Engineering for a feasibility read before clinical review time is spent on it.
